subject: Scope vs Band Review for Senior ML Offer
messages:
From: Alex Mueller <alex.mueller@acme-analytics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: New candidate: Sofia Ramos — senior ML hire (scope question)

Mina,

Thanks for the quick chat earlier. Per our discussion, we're ready to extend an offer to Sofia Ramos for the Senior ML Engineer slot on the Acme Analytics integration team. Before we finalize comp, I wanted to flag scope that may justify a higher band: she would be owning model infra for a cross-product feature, mentoring two ICs, and driving the initial production rollout.

Candidate details attached: SofiaRamos_Resume.pdf and the role JD (senior_ml_jd.pdf). Proposed starting band from the recruiting brief is L5. Hiring manager is pushing for L6 because this role has product leadership elements. Can the leveling committee confirm whether we should present L5 or L6 for the offer?

Key asks:
- Leveling recommendation (L5 vs L6) and justification
- If L5, can we make a band-top offer (base + equity) to bridge scope?
- Any additional documentation required for an exception?

Timing: Manager hopes to have a signed offer by next week (target 7/17).

Appreciate the help — happy to hop on a 20-min sync if easier.

— Alex Mueller
Director, Talent Partnerships
Acme Analytics
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mueller <alex.mueller@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: New candidate: Sofia Ramos — senior ML hire (scope question)

Alex — thanks, and great summary. I reviewed Sofia's resume and the JD. A couple quick thoughts:

- The cross-product ownership + mentoring leans toward L6 responsibilities, but our bar for L6 at Redwood typically includes sustained cross-org influence or leading multiple product/infra planks.
- If the manager is clear this is a one-person critical launch, an L5 with top-of-band comp + 6-month review for accelerated leveling is a pragmatic path.

Requesting leveling committee input — tagging Jonas and Laura for formal guidance. Attaching comp_band_chart_Q3.pdf for reference on top-of-band parameters.

For the committee: please confirm whether we should present L5 (with top-of-band) or make an exception to extend L6 on offer. If recommending L5, please indicate suggested base % and equity tier to propose.

Mina Haddad
Recruiting Lead, Engineering Hiring
Redwood Inference
Attachment: comp_band_chart_Q3.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 10:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Leveling committee recommendation — Sofia Ramos (recap)

Team,

Quick recap from the committee review today. We pulled Sofia's resume, manager feedback, and the role JD. Summary points and recommendation below: 

Summary:
- Scope: owner of infra for a new cross-product feature, mentoring 1–2 ICs, single-team product cadence but cross-org dependencies.
- Impact: high near-term impact for product launch, but limited history of org-wide influence in prior roles.
- Candidate seniority: strong technical depth and systems design; limited evidence of multi-team leadership.

Recommendation (consensus):
- Offer as L5 (Senior) with an exception-style packet: top-of-band base + elevated equity Tier 2.
- Include a formal 6-month performance checkpoint with clear success metrics that, if met, will trigger an expedited leveling review to L6.

Rationale: L6 should remain reserved for candidates with demonstrable cross-org leadership and a track record of shaping multiple roadmaps. Sofia's current profile meets many L6 signals but not consistently. The top-of-band + expedited review balances managerial needs and our leveling rigor.

Suggested numbers (guideline):
- Base: 95th percentile of L5 band (region-adjusted)
- Equity: move from standard L5 Tier 1 to Tier 2 grant size
- Sign-on: $20k one-time to recognize relocation/market pressure

If you want the committee to authorize an outright L6 offer, we need: written manager case with measurable cross-org deliverables + 2 internal stakeholder endorsements (product lead and infra lead).

Attaching: leveling_committee_notes.pdf (short notes + vote).

— Jonas Weber
Director, Talent Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mueller <alex.mueller@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Leveling committee recommendation — Sofia Ramos (offer plan)

Alex — forwarding the committee decision and suggested offer structure. TL;DR: we should present Sofia with an L5 (Senior) offer but make it top-of-band with elevated equity and a $20k sign-on, plus an accelerated 6-month leveling review that could move her to L6 if predefined outcomes are met.

Proposed next steps for offer package: 
- Base: 95th percentile of L5 comp band (region-adjusted)
- Equity: L5 Tier 2 grant
- Sign-on: $20,000 one-time
- Manager to provide 3 measurable outcomes for the 6-month checkpoint (deployment SLA, mentorship milestones, and cross-team integration milestones)

Alex, can you confirm that the hiring manager is comfortable with the 6-month checkpoint and whether Acme will accept an L5 with expedited review versus an immediate L6? If manager still strongly prefers L6, we can collect the two endorsements and a short manager memo and re-submit for exception.

I will prepare the offer docs once you confirm and will attach the offer template (Redwood offer packet) and the committee notes.

Thanks — Mina
Recruiting Lead, Engineering Hiring
Redwood Inference
